t: 3791. Number of Balanced Integers in a Range
o: A balanced integer has at least two digits and equal sums of digits at odd and even positions, counting position 1 from the left. Between 1 and 100 the nine repdigits 11..99 qualify; in [120,129] only 121 works; 1234 fails (4 vs 6). With bounds up to 1e15 this is a textbook digit DP: count balanced numbers <= X via a tight-constrained walk over X's digits, then answer f(high) - f(low - 1). Leading zeros must not occupy positions, so track a 'started' flag; a single started digit can never balance (its difference is nonzero), so 'started and diff == 0' correctly enforces the two-digit minimum.
k: Digit DP over X's digits with state (position, signed alternating sum difference, started, tight).
Position parity is relative to the number itself: while not started, leading zeros do not toggle parity.
f(high) - f(low-1) answers the range query; low >= 1 keeps things simple.
Single-digit numbers can never satisfy diff = 0 once started, so no separate length flag is needed.

a.i: Walk the digits of X left to right. At each position choose a digit <= the tight bound; once started, add/subtract the digit from a running difference depending on position parity. Memoize on (pos, diff, started, tight); count endpoints with started and diff = 0.
s: Define f(X): memoized DP over the decimal digits of X.
Transition: if not started, choosing 0 stays not-started; choosing d > 0 starts the number with diff = d (position 1, odd).
If started, diff += d at even indexes (odd positions) and diff -= d at odd indexes (even positions).
At the end return 1 iff started and diff == 0; answer = f(high) - f(low - 1).
a.t: O(D * D * 9 * 4) per f-call where D <= 17 digits - effectively constant; two calls total
a.sp: O(D^2) memo table (positions x difference range)

w: Digit DP is the only viable family here; spend interview time on the 'started' flag and parity convention. Pitfalls: applying parity to leading zeros (shifts every position), forgetting the at-least-two-digits rule (handled implicitly), and off-by-one on f(low - 1). Follow-up: count balanced numbers with a given digit sum, or balanced numbers in another base.
